title: Run result envelope
description: What every run returns, discovery or replay. A common envelope with a status-specific payload, machine-readable throughout — the caller is an AI agent, not a human reading prose. The four statuses are the whole contract: a caller that handles all four has handled everything the system can do.

mode.description: Which path produced this result. Load-bearing: replay is constrained below to zero model calls, so the central claim of the system is enforced by the contract rather than asserted in prose.

status.description: Recoverable conditions are deliberately absent: a retried slow load or a dismissed known interstitial is logged in the trace and never becomes a terminal status.

inputs.description: Parameters this run was invoked with, echoed back so a result is self-contained.

llm_call_count.description: Counted, not estimated. Asserted zero on every replay.

app_fingerprint_observed.description: What the app reported at run time. Compared against the artifact's recorded value; absent means the app did not report one (a crashed app cannot), which is 'unknown', never 'unchanged'.

drift_warning.description: Present when the observed fingerprint differs from the recorded one. A warning, not a failure: most app changes do not touch the flow that was recorded.

intervention_record.description: Present on the final result of any run that paused for a human, whatever its terminal status.

then.description: Replay is the production path and takes no model in the decision loop. A replay result carrying a non-zero count is not a warning, it is an invalid document.

success_payload.description: Typed outputs exactly as the artifact declared them. No prose.

checkpoint_verified.description: SUCCESS is only reachable with a verified checkpoint, so this can only be true. Kept explicit so the caller sees the claim rather than inferring it.

business_outcome_payload.description: A first-class answer the caller branches on, not an error.

needs_intervention_payload.description: A live pause, forward-looking: someone must act now. Carries enough context to act without reading the trace.

reason.description: Why control was handed over. AGENT_STUCK is discovery-only; the rest are replay. MUTATION_NOT_APPROVED and IRREVERSIBLE_STEP are distinct on purpose — the first is answerable by re-invoking with standing approval, the second never is.

session_id.description: The live browser session the human takes over. Required: the human operates the session the automation was using, never a fresh one.

requested_action.description: What the operator is being asked to do, and what state means it is done.

control.description: Single writer at a time, tracked explicitly.

hard_failure_payload.description: Maximum debuggability, and deliberately no remediation field. If the engine knew the fix it would be a recoverable condition, so a suggestion here would be a guess wearing the costume of an instruction — additionalProperties:false makes adding one a schema error.

strategies_tried.description: Every locator strategy attempted, in order. Distinguishes 'the element moved' from 'the page was wrong'.

intervention_record.description: What happened while a human held control. Written on resume so the audit trail covers the manual segment too, not just the automated one. A list rather than a single entry: a capability with both a mutating and an irreversible step pauses twice unattended, and a run can pause repeatedly on one step when an operator resumes without having changed anything — discarding those loses exactly the entries an audit exists to keep.

operator.description: Who took over. Per run rather than per pause: the same person answers the prompt they are sitting at.

when.description: Where the pause sits relative to the action, because the two resume differently. A risk gate pauses before_step: the step has not run, so resuming runs it. A dialog or expired session pauses after_step: the step ran, so resuming re-judges the page it landed on and never re-sends the action.

decision.description: What the operator answered. 'abandon' includes there having been no console to ask, which is deliberate: an unattended run does not get to approve its own mutations, and the record should not imply someone declined.

resolution.description: How the handoff ended. This is what makes 'never blind-resume' auditable rather than merely implemented: an operator who answered without acting leaves a paused_again behind. 'verified' means a checkpoint was re-checked and held; 'resumed' means control came back and the run continued with no checkpoint to re-check, which is every discovery handoff, since a flow still being discovered has none yet. The two are separate so the record never claims a verification that did not happen.

human_actions.description: Observed state transitions while control was HUMAN — captured, not self-reported. One entry per handoff: the engine is blocked on the operator while they work, and instrumenting the page to record keystrokes would capture credentials into the trace, which §8 makes structurally impossible everywhere else. Full before/after DOM snapshots live in evidence; this carries the summary.

post_resume_checkpoint.description: Re-verified before continuing. Never blind-resume: if this fails the run pauses again rather than acting on an assumed state. Absent when the operator abandoned, and when the step resumed into declares no checkpoint of its own.
